findings.reason: The protected Fenwick helpers repeatedly use the prohibited local name index. The inert candidate preserves the exact empty-slot algorithm and app-local contract while using conventional n, i, and j variables for the tree extent, accumulated prefix position, and binary-lifting probe.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 406 and its Python reconstructQueue surface. The Reference preserves the height-and-k meaning, multiplicity of people, valid-reconstruction guarantee, both source examples in order with the supplied explanation complete, and all four constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064725574 and uses the same ascending-height/decreasing-k sort, Fenwick initialization, order-statistic search, slot placement, and removal as the protected app-local source. The candidate is inert and changes only local names.

The legal 64-, 192-, and 512-person tiers span 8x and force repeated front placement for the quadratic alternative. The candidate passes all 11 executions at +0.01 relative growth and 0.99x. Python's native list.insert hides shifts in optimized C and remains below the runtime threshold at these legal sizes, but the independently expressed equivalent algorithm with explicit shifts passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.86 and 5.88x.

The Approach exactly derives the ascending-height and decreasing-k order, maps each k value to the (k + 1)th empty slot, explains Fenwick binary lifting and removal, proves the invariant for already placed shorter people and future taller people, and states O(n log n) time with O(n) space.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples, the complete first reconstruction explanation, exact greater-than-or-equal counting semantics, occurrence multiplicity, valid-input guarantee, and all four constraints.
